items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: Teddy Wilson still thrills me, just the exuberance of his playing when he was playing in the 1930s on the Billie Holiday records and some of the Benny Goodman small band sextet records.

ctx.x: Well, good work. Who are your — do you have piano heroes?

Yeah I do. The first thing that comes into my mind is Jimmy Rowles. I’ve always been crazy about his playing, ever since I heard the records he made in the 1940s, I was crazy about his playing. And when I finally met him years later, he didn’t disappoint me. He was just — he’d even become a greater piano player than I even knew about. He was my favorite. Mel Powell knocked me out. I loved the way he articulated his music. It was beautiful. Teddy Wilson still thrills me, just the exuberance of his playing when he…
I know. When you listen to that you just say that’s not possible. How could you think that fast and then play that fast.
